note: School Trips' uncertainty table: one row per model input and causal link, with its source or "judgment", its low and high, and the data test it passed. site/scripts/check-assumptions.mjs fails on a row with no source, low or high, and reruns the All Changes headline at each row's low and high to print its share. param names the makeCityModel P.assume key (or cost.<COSTS key>, or case for the sim's three cases); rerun is light (the page's model reruns it), alone (the change's own low and high from makeCityModel's alone(), standing in for a rerun), sim (needs scripts/school-sim.py, not rerun here) or none (a measured figure). studies are ids in data/evidence/studies.json. reread.finding: Reread at 39% of the kids hurt headline (kokka-2024, elvik-2009-speed, wales-20mph-2025). The central 10% holds: Edinburgh measured 10% fewer casualties (95% CI 0% to 19%) from a signs-only limit that moved mean speed 1.3 mph, and Elvik's injured-people exponent of 1.4 gives 5% to 10% at a 1 to 2 mph drop, the size a part-day school zone limit can expect. The 25% high is the weak end: it comes from Wales's first year, with no control group and a 3.8 mph mean speed drop, graded a size mismatch. Edinburgh's own interval would put the high at 19%.

reread.finding: Reread 2026-10-22 at 35% of the yearly cost headline, once the private schools joined the run: the $25,000 to $60,000 swing adds $5.7M a year, so about 163 schools carry the program. The high reproduces from Perez-Martin et al. 2018 (perez-martin-2018-cordoba): EUR 8,350 over 59 days at EUR 13 an hour is about 11 monitor hours a day, and at $30 an hour for 180 days that is $58,800. The central $25,000 and the volunteer low of $5,000 have no cost figure behind them in the rows they cite: johnson-2024 records the trial's effect but no cost, so the central is our judgment and stays one.
